newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Wednesday on overnight gains on the London Metals Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,300 yuan ($2,444) per tonne, rising 170 yuan. It opened at 20,300 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 20,280 and a high of 20,370.
October rose 70 to 20,770, November 70 to 20,520, December 180 to 20,350, February 190 to 20,330 and March 160 to 20,330.
Combined volume rose to 41,310 tonnes from 19,510.
Copper opened higher and moved in a narrow range at high levels for most of the session.
Traders said the LME gains triggered short-covering from retail investors but institutions did not want to lift prices sharply due to uncertainties over the short-term trend.
"LME gains discouraged short position holders and many individuals offset their short positions," one trader said.
"But long position holders had no confidence to push contracts above the 20,400 yuan level due to unclear short-term direction," he added.
Traders said domestic spot demand did not increase and copper will meet strong hedge-selling when it rises.
"Copper is not likely to breach the range of 20,000 and 20,500 in the short term unless there is unexpected news," a second trader said.
Some traders said copper would fall again after a technical rebound due to poor mid- and long-term fundamentals.
Aluminium ended little changed. September was unchanged at 13,930, October rose 200 to 14,000 and November was flat at 14,000. Combined volume fell to 500 tonnes from 870.
